title: Gupta administration
note: The early baseline represents Gupta-period administration; evidence is strongest in fifth–sixth-century grants. The fourth-century extent is uncertain.

title: Bhutivarman acquires Paundravardhana
note: Adopted expansion episode. The acquisition and its extent are reconstructed; Barganga does not supply a conquest date.

title: Lost after Mahasenagupta’s victory
note: Adopted loss under Susthitavarman. The defeat is reported; transfer of this entire river-bounded sector is the map interpretation.

title: Bhaskaravarman recovers the western territory
note: Adopted recovery during Bhaskaravarman’s western expansion. His Karnasuvarna camp is attested; recovery of this sector and its year are inferred.

title: Control after Bhaskaravarman uncertain
note: The end of Bhaskaravarman’s western possession is not securely dated. The neutral fill marks a gap in the adopted sequence.

title: Harshadeva’s Gauda lordship
note: Adopted lordship phase, using c.735 for playback. The Pasupati claim does not specify a dated reconquest of this entire region.

title: Western control uncertain
note: No uninterrupted ownership is inferred from Harshadeva’s claim. Bengal records also claim submission by a Pragjyotisha ruler during Devapala’s reign.

title: Vanamala reasserts authority
note: Adopted recovery under Vanamalavarman, based on the disputed North Bengal identification of grant geography.

title: Control before Ratnapala’s western victory uncertain
note: The founding of the Kamarupa Pala line does not itself establish recovery of the whole sector.

title: Ratnapala defeats Rajyapala
note: Adopted acquisition following the reported Gauda victory and Ganges advance. The year is a playback reference within his approximate reign.

title: Chandra counter-campaign
note: Adopted reversal associated with Srichandra’s Kamarupa campaign. The exact date and possession of this entire sector are not specified by the record.

title: Indrapala restores western authority
note: Adopted recovery after the victory over Kalyanachandra. The fill is carried forward as a scenario assumption; intervening administration was contested.

title: Jatavarman takes the territory
note: Adopted loss to Jatavarman. His Kamarupa adversary and the exact parcel are uncertain; this display avoids pairing him with Harshapala’s incompatible early reign dates.

title: Dharmapala recovers the territory
note: User-adopted recovery episode. A primary reconquest passage and consistent absolute chronology have not been established; c.1090 is an illustrative playback date.
